- When sentiment is consistently bullish (positive) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast decline after peak to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment turns bearish (negative) within 3–5 days, model should adjust downward with a lag — don’t react immediately to sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% to align with historical reversion.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast with 3–5 day moving average to reduce volatility.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, model is overconfident — reduce forecast by 3–7% for next period unless sentiment confirms bullish momentum.
